children: Shares of ICICI Bank touched a fresh 52-week high of ₹1,616 on the NSE on Wednesday before trimming gains, trading at ₹1,577.70, down 0.71 per cent from Monday’s close of ₹1,589, as of 12.43 pm. The stock opened at its intraday peak and has since pulled back, with sell orders dominating at 68.34 per cent of total order flow against 31.66 per cent on the buy side. Traded volume stood at 184.92 lakh shares, with a traded value of ₹2,959.58 crore by early afternoon. The bank’s market capitalisation stood at over ₹11.33 lakh crore.

The momentum follows a string of bullish analyst calls. Morgan Stanley has added ICICI Bank to both its Asia ex-Japan and GEM Focus Lists, citing a growth-supportive rate cycle and attractive valuations. The American brokerage views the bank as solid and defensive amid market volatility and expects it to sustain strong balance sheet growth and profitability.

title: ICICI Bank hits 52-week high before retreating; Morgan Stanley adds to focus list
